title: Topic 3.8.2: Parable of the mustard seed

pages.lesson:
LESSON: PARABLE OF THE MUSTARD SEED

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: The Life of Jesus Christ
Topic 3.8.2: Parable of the mustard seed

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Parable of the mustard seed. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How does the parable of the mustard seed relate to the kingdom of God?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. retell the parable of the mustard seed as guided by the Bible text
2. describe how the kingdom of God grows from a small beginning
3. explain how they contribute to the growth of the kingdom of God
4. appreciate the growth of God’s kingdom by evangelising to others

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: PARABLE OF THE MUSTARD SEED
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Parable of the mustard seed helps you succeed in CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS ABOUT PLANTS
Roots hold the plant and take in water. Leaves help the plant make food using sunlight.
Kenyan examples: maize, beans, sukuma wiki, bananas, mango trees.
Without water and light, most seedlings wilt.

PART 1: Retell the parable of the mustard seed as guided by the Bible text

What this means
In this part you learn to retell the parable of the mustard seed as guided by the Bible text. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: retell the parable of the mustard seed as guided by the Bible text.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Parable of the mustard seed” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can retell the parable of the mustard seed as guided by the Bible text. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Describe how the kingdom of God grows from a small beginning

What this means
In this part you learn to describe how the kingdom of God grows from a small beginning. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe how the kingdom of God grows from a small beginning.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Parable of the mustard seed in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe how the kingdom of God grows from a small beginning. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Explain how they contribute to the growth of the kingdom of God

What this means
In this part you learn to explain how they contribute to the growth of the kingdom of God. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain how they contribute to the growth of the kingdom of God.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain how they contribute to the growth of the kingdom of God. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Appreciate the growth of God’s kingdom by evangelising to others

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the growth of God’s kingdom by evangelising to others. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the growth of God’s kingdom by evangelising to others.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Parable of the mustard seed” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the growth of God’s kingdom by evangelising to others. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Parable of the mustard seed is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Roots hold the plant and take in water. Leaves help the plant make food using sunlight.

Kenyan examples: maize, beans, sukuma wiki, bananas, mango trees.

Example 1: Show how “Parable of the mustard seed” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: retell the parable of the mustard seed as guided by the Bible text)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Parable of the mustard seed in your own words. (skill: describe how the kingdom of God grows from a small beginning)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: explain how they contribute to the growth of the kingdom of God)

Example 4: Show how “Parable of the mustard seed” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: appreciate the growth of God’s kingdom by evangelising to others)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Parable of the mustard seed to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: retell the parable of the mustard seed as guided by the Bible text.
3. Practise this skill: describe how the kingdom of God grows from a small beginning.
4. Practise this skill: explain how they contribute to the growth of the kingdom of God.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Parable of the mustard seed from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Parable of the mustard seed: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Parable of the mustard seed?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How does the parable of the mustard seed relate to the kingdom of God?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Parable of the mustard seed means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: retell the parable of the mustard seed as guided by the Bible text.
5. Be able to: describe how the kingdom of God grows from a small beginning.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
